channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Womanhood · Photobook Cafe & Rapid Eye Darkroom
item.description: Sixth quarterly open call from Photobook Cafe and Rapid Eye Darkrooms exploring the theme of Womanhood with guest judge Francesca Allen. Invites work exploring the lived experiences of women and those who identify with womanhood — friendship, sisterhood, identity, growth, vulnerability, resistance, and becoming. Open to anyone, emerging, established or amateur, any age, background and identity from anywhere in the world. 35 selected photographers will be featured in a group exhibition and zine publication at The Photobook Cafe in London. — Deadline: April 20, 2026. Fee: £25. Prize: Exhibition + zine publication.

item.title: 43rd Center Annual · Houston Center for Photography
item.description: Houston Center for Photography's annual group exhibition, now in its 43rd year. Seeks to highlight current themes, technologies, and practices in photography. Features diverse works from HCP members worldwide — emerging, mid-career, and established photographers. Two artists selected for $500 HCP Juried Membership Honoraria. This year juried by Asha Iman Veal, curator for globally collaborative exhibitions of contemporary art. Exhibition runs June 4 – August 16, 2026. — Deadline: April 19, 2026. Fee: $35 (membership required). Prize: Two $500 honoraria + exhibition.

item.title: Golden Turtle International Wildlife Festival 2026
item.description: International wildlife photography competition in 12 categories: Animals in the Environment, Portrait of the Animal, Animal Behaviour, Microcosm, Underwater World, Art and Nature's Image, Landscape, Magic of Plants, Humans and Nature, Reserved Russia, Mobile Photography, and Youth (two age groups). Up to 20 photos per author. Professional jury of international wildlife photographers. Finalists exhibited in Moscow autumn 2026, published in festival album. No zoo photography except Humans and Nature category. No composites or montage. RAW files required from semifinalists. — Deadline: April 7, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: ~$1,500 grand prize + ~$750 per category + trophy + album.

item.title: Nikon Comedy Wildlife Photography Awards 2026
item.description: Annual international competition celebrating the funniest moments in wildlife photography. Founded in 2015 by Paul Joynson-Hicks and Tom Sullam. Free to enter, open to everyone worldwide with any camera brand. Nine categories: Mammals, Birds, Reptiles/Amphibians/Insects, Fish & Aquatic Species, Nikon Young Photographer, Nikon Junior, Portfolio, Nikon Video, and People's Choice Award. Grand prize: week-long safari for two at Alex Walker's Serian in the Maasai Mara, Kenya. Category winners receive Nikon cameras and lenses plus handmade trophies. Over 10,000 entries from 100+ countries. Proceeds support wildlife conservation. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Kenya safari for 2 + Nikon gear + trophies.

item.title: FLORA — Shutter Hub Editions Photobook
item.description: Open call for a printed photobook celebrating the diversity, resilience, subtleties, and poetry of growing things. Images should capture vegetation from mosses and ferns to forests, blossoms, vines, and roots — revealing the nuance of growth, patterns of nature's processes, and the quiet power of plant life in all environments. Selected images featured in a printed FLORA photobook, available through shutterhub.org.uk and selected stockists. Pay-what-you-can entry with £15 minimum donation. Free submissions available for photographers with limited income (email request required before entry). AI use must be disclosed. — Deadline: June 11, 2026. Fee: £15+. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Hidden Narratives Residency 2026 · Photoworks / Royal Geographical Society
item.description: Year-long residency (2026–2027) for Italian photographers to immerse in the historic collections of the Royal Geographical Society in London. In partnership with the Italian Cultural Institute in London. Artists engage with archival materials relating to the environment and humanitarian themes, developing presentations and works around hidden narratives, loss, and human impact. Applicants should have experience in photographic archive research. Interviews on April 27, 2026. — Deadline: April 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Year-long residency at Royal Geographical Society.

item.title: Hasselblad Foundation Nature Photography Grant 2026
item.description: Grant for photographic explorations of nature, landscape, and environment. Emphasis on originality, environmental issues, biodiversity, and human impact on nature and climate. Open to citizens of Nordic countries or permanent residents of the Nordic region. Projects should have a 1–3 year timeframe. — Deadline: May 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 100,000 SEK grant.

item.title: Guest Room: Shana Lopes & Aspen Mays · Der Greif
item.description: Open call curated by Shana Lopes (Assistant Curator of Photography, SFMOMA) and Aspen Mays (Associate Professor/Chair of Photography, California College of the Arts) exploring the theme "A Little Bit of Magic" — inviting work that engages with doubling, substitution, sleight of hand, constructed realities, staged impossibilities, and illusion in photography. Open to everyone. Selected work featured on Der Greif's platform with feedback session from the curators. — Deadline: April 2, 2026. Fee: Voluntary. Prize: Feature on Der Greif + feedback session + €250 scholarship.

item.title: Photobook Feature — In Focus · Der Greif
item.description: Open call for photobooks to be featured in Der Greif's Articles section with a dedicated editorial write-up. No fixed theme. Seeks photobooks demonstrating strong conceptual thinking, thoughtful sequencing, and an engaged relationship to the medium of the book. Accepts self-published photobooks, artist books, zines, experimental publications, and small-edition press titles. Both recent releases and unpublished or in-progress projects eligible (if publication-ready). — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Voluntary. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Jugend fotografiert Deutschland 2025 · laif foundation
item.description: German youth photography contest for ages 10–18, now in its 2025/26 edition. Theme: "Be you. Be seen. Be heard." Submit documentary photo stories on any personally relevant topic. Smartphones or cameras welcome, no prior experience required. Individuals or teams of up to 10 participants with optional coaches from schools, youth centers, or community organizations. Must be residents of Germany. — Deadline: April 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €200–€500 + exhibition.

item.title: RESTART2026 · Lithuanian Photographers' Association
item.description: International photography competition and exhibition for photographers starting their careers or reconsidering their creative direction with new work. Submit a series of 10–20 photographs created after 2021 that has not been fully exhibited or published. 10 finalists exhibit at Prospekto gallery in Vilnius. Top 3 winners receive individual exhibitions at Vilnius Photography Gallery the following year with partial production support. Printed catalogue for finalists. Featured on photography.lt and screened at NIDA Meeting Photography symposium in September. — Deadline: April 12, 2026. Fee: €15. Prize: Solo exhibition + catalogue.

item.title: DPPF 2026 Sports Photography Grants
item.description: Grants supporting emerging and early-career sports photographers with fewer than 3 years cumulative paid professional sports photography experience. Seven photographers receive $5,000 each for career development plus expenses-paid trip to the Sports Photography Gathering (September 16–18, 2026). Up to 3 winners eligible for year-long mentorship with Advisory Board members. Up to 3 additional applicants receive $2,500 Development Grants. Open worldwide except countries under active US sanctions. — Deadline: May 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 7 × $5,000 + 3 × $2,500 + mentorship.

item.title: Bowness Photography Prize 2026
item.description: Australia's richest photography prize, now in its 20th year. Open to Australian citizens or permanent residents (12+ months). Winner receives $50,000 AUD and acquisition into MAPh's permanent collection. Two Honourable Mentions receive $2,500 each. Wai Tang Commissioning Award of $10,000 for a future exhibition. People's Choice Award of $5,000. Finalists exhibited at MAPh gallery. Accepts still photo-based media including analogue and digital photography produced within the past year. Up to 3 works per $55 entry. AI permitted only if not the substantial or overriding input. Entries open April 16, 2026. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $55 AUD. Prize: $50,000 + $10,000 + $5,000 + 2 × $2,500.

item.title: Home · Photography 4 Humanity
item.description: Global open call exploring the theme of home — safety, belonging, dignity, identity, and place. In partnership with Fotografiska Emerging and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. Selected works will be exhibited at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Human Rights Day, December 10, 2026. Curated by James Nachtwey and Pauline Benthede (Fotografiska Global VP Artistic Direction). Open to emerging photographers worldwide. 31 artists selected: 1 main image, 10 runner-ups, 20 honorable mentions. All forms of lens-based photography welcome, analog or digital. AI-generated or prompt-based images not accepted. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exibart Street Photography Contest — 5th Edition
item.description: Fifth edition of the international street photography contest by Exibart Street, Italy's leading contemporary art magazine. Two categories: Best Single Photo (€10) and Best Series of 3–9 images (€49). Winners receive a Leica Q3 or Xiaomi 17 Ultra with Leica lenses, plus interviews and editorial coverage across the Exibart network. Sponsored by Leica Camera. Open to photographers worldwide. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: €10–€49. Prize: Leica Q3 + Xiaomi 17 Ultra + publication.

item.title: Flanelle Print No. 47 — July 2026
item.description: Montreal-based fashion and arts magazine (est. 2012) accepting submissions for Print No. 47, publishing July 2026. Open to artists, photographers, and designers worldwide. Selected work featured in quarterly print and digital magazine with international distribution. Two-phase review process. Work must be unpublished and exclusive to Flanelle. Paid upgrade options available for cover placement and priority publishing. — Deadline: June 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Embracing Our Differences 2027 Outdoor Exhibition
item.description: International outdoor juried exhibition in its 23rd year. 50 selected artworks are displayed as billboard-sized panels (16 ft × 12.5 ft) in public parks in Sarasota and St. Petersburg, Florida, from January to April 2027. Three awards: $2,000 Best-in-Show Adult, $2,000 Best-in-Show Student, $2,000 People's Choice. Work must reflect themes of diversity, inclusion, kindness, and respect. Accepts photography, painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art. Horizontal orientation only. No limit on entries per artist. 150-word artist statement required. Over 5.2 million visitors since 2004. AI-generated work not accepted. — Deadline: July 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,000 Best-in-Show + $2,000 Student + $2,000 People's Choice.

item.title: Ephemere Photo Journal Vol. 2 — Triplicities
item.description: Submit text-driven photo features exploring "Triplicities: The Magic of Three" — Time's Arrow, The Life Cycle, The Dialectic. Accepted formats include personal essays, critical essays, photo-poetry, philosophical explorations, interviews, and reviews. Published in a collectible large-format newsprint journal printed in Japan. Shortlisted authors work directly with editors in a collaborative editing process. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: ¥10,000 + publication.

item.title: European Landscapes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call for photographs of European landscapes — lakes, rivers, sea, trees, sunsets, storms, gardens. Selected work published in a printed photo book. No collage, manipulated, or AI-generated photos accepted. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Northern Europe Landscapes Open Call · Soft Publishing
item.description: Open call for photographs of northern European natural and rural landscapes (no buildings). Selected work published in a printed photo book. No collage, manipulated, or AI-generated photos accepted. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: KH7 Artspace — Exhibitions 2026
item.description: Open call for solo or group exhibition proposals at KH7 Artspace in Aarhus, Denmark for the second half of 2026. Available slots: December at KH7Artspace, September and November at KH7Smallspace. All artistic disciplines welcome including photography. Artists receive a small fee and PR support. Applicants from outside Denmark must cover their own transport and visa expenses. Submit project description (max 2 A4 pages with images) via email. — Deadline: March 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + artist fee + PR support.

item.title: Fresh Legs 2026 · Galleri Heike Arndt DK
item.description: Annual group exhibition initiative running since 2013, presenting painting, sculpture, illustration, drawing, street art, photography, short film, animation, and related media. Exhibition at two Berlin venues: Galleri Heike Arndt DK (June–October 2026) and INSELGALERIE Berlin (June–July 2026). No submission fee; €40 exhibition fee if accepted. Selected works must remain available for 12 months for potential follow-up exhibitions. All works must be for sale. Gallery takes 30–50% commission on sales. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: I Can Buy Myself Flowers · Haze Gallery
item.description: HAZEGALLERY, the curatorial platform of PURPLEHAZE Magazine, invites artists and image-makers to participate in a curated pop-up exhibition in Amsterdam alongside the launch of PURPLEHAZE Print Issue 012. Theme explores autonomy as identity, rituals of independence, intimacy turned inward, beauty chosen rather than granted, solitude as clarity, and desire as self-directed. Accepts fashion, fine art, and documentary photography, works on paper, fine art prints, and short looping video works. Selected artists participate in the June 2026 Amsterdam exhibition and may be published in the print issue. — Deadline: April 16, 2026. Fee: €35. Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Les Mots du Phare Vol. 04: Futur(s) · Linea Recta Books
item.description: Open call for black-and-white photography for Vol. 04 of Les Mots du Phare, a print publication by Linea Recta Books and Le Phare Collectif. Theme: Futur(s) — imagining what seems impossible, a tomorrow, an after, a continuation. Not the end of the world, but the courage to imagine what is possible. Selected images will be featured in the printed edition alongside text contributions from members of the collective. Submit up to 4 B&W photos combined into one PDF via email. — Deadline: April 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Night Aesthetics · Fotografiska
item.description: Open call exploring the visual world of the night. Looking for works that engage with light, movement, atmosphere, intimacy, and the energy that appears when the day lets go. Whether captured on a crowded dance floor, in a quiet street, or somewhere in between. Welcomes lens-based photography in all forms including analog and digital. Three winners each receive €2,500 and feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. In partnership with Jägermeister. — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × €2,500.

item.title: The 2026 Lumen Prize
item.description: Leading international award for art created with technology, now in its 15th year. Three categories: Legacy Futures, Systems & Structures, and Experiential Innovation, each with a $5,000 prize. The Jury also selects one Gold Award Winner receiving $15,000. Works may include film, photography, AI-generated art, interactive installations, VR experiences, and more. Finalists announced August, winners announced November. Awards ceremony at Kunstsilo Museum in Norway. — Deadline: May 23, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: $30,000.

item.title: Nest — Group Exhibition · Fringe Arts Bath
item.description: Group exhibition exploring how creative practice nurtures wellbeing, inspires reflection, or aids recovery. Open call for art created in response to lived experience of mental health, disability, or health journey. All mediums welcome including photography, painting, film, sculpture, ceramics, poetry, and installation. Curated by photographic artist Livvy Eden. Exhibition runs 22 May – 6 June 2026 at 103 Walcot Street, Bath. Selected artists asked for £25 participation donation. — Deadline: April 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Michael P. Smith Fund for Documentary Photography 2025 · New Orleans Photo Alliance
item.description: Annual grant honoring legendary New Orleans documentary photographer Michael P. Smith. Awards cash prizes and exhibition opportunities to Gulf Coast photographers whose work combines artistic excellence and a sustained commitment to a cultural documentary project. Open to photographers residing in Gulf Coast states: Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and Florida. Subject matter not limited to Gulf Coast region. Grant winner receives $3,000, PhotoNOLA Portfolio Review access, NOPA Palladium membership, and exhibition. Two honorable mentions receive Portfolio reviews and membership. Top 10 finalists listed on NOPA website. Winner donates two prints to NOPA permanent collection. — Deadline: May 4, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $3,000 + portfolio review + exhibition.

item.title: Monograph No. 01 · No-Type Magazine
item.description: Open call for lens-based artists to submit a cohesive photographic project for an individual artist monograph. The selected artist receives full publication support including editing, design, printing, and marketing, plus 20% of the edition. Shortlist of 6 artists announced June 8; they receive published interviews. All submitted artists considered for Editor's Choice issue and digital features. — Deadline: May 31, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 37th Annual Juried Photography Show · State of the Art Gallery
item.description: Annual juried photography show in Ithaca, NY. Up to $1,000 in prizes awarded at judge's discretion. Original work not previously exhibited at the gallery is accepted across all photographic media. Post-production manipulation acceptable if based on original photographic process. Images wholly produced by AI are not acceptable. Accepted works must be matted, framed, and ready to hang. 30% commission on sales. Exhibition May 28 – June 27, 2026. Awards ceremony June 5. — Deadline: May 1, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Homo Technologicus · LoosenArt
item.description: International call exploring the relationship between humans and technology. Seeking works investigating social, environmental, physical, cognitive, and emotional transformations brought by digital innovation. Group exhibition in Rome, November 2026. — Deadline: July 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Residency Program 2026 · Aurora PhotoCenter
item.description: One residency for artists working in photography or photo-based media at Herron School of Art + Design. Two-week intensive work period (August 10–21, 2026, fixed dates). $1,000 stipend plus up to $500 travel reimbursement. Includes darkroom facility, studios, and basic chemistry. Housing on CAMi campus for out-of-town residents. Resident must give a talk during or after the residency. Previous Aurora exhibitors (2025–2026) ineligible. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: $10 (via Slideroom). Prize: $1,000 stipend + $500 travel + residency.

item.title: People 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International photography call exploring the human figure across all approaches including portraits, documentary, street photography, and studio work. Diverse interpretations welcome whether posed or unposed, observed or imagined. Selected work displayed in online exhibition. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: €7 per image. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Nature 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Exhibition exploring how we interact with nature. Seeking images that reveal beauty, power, cruelty, and influence on daily life. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026. — Deadline: March 27, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Future Days 2026 · Glasgow Gallery of Photography
item.description: Open theme exhibition asking photographers to represent their vision of the future, whether hopeful or fearful. Interpret the theme at a global, local, or personal level. Selected work displayed in Glasgow gallery, online gallery, and exhibition catalogue. Exhibition runs July 3-31, 2026. — Deadline: March 27, 2026. Fee: Free (£48 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: Artist in Residence Program 2026 · TILT Institute
item.description: Four-week residency for artists advancing contemporary photography. Two artists selected: one slot for a Philadelphia-based artist, one open to all. Includes $3,000 honorarium, waived printer/scanner fees, $1,000 ink and paper credit, and $1,500 travel/housing reimbursement. Residencies run June through November 2026. — Deadline: March 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,000 + residency.

item.title: Outside the Box: Cameraless Photography · PhotoSynthesis
item.description: Exhibition seeking photographic works incorporating cameraless techniques including photograms, chemigrams, lumen prints, chlorophyll prints, phytograms, anthotypes, cyanotypes, and composites blending camera and non-camera methods. 30–40 pieces selected for gallery exhibition (May 30 – July 11, 2026) and website display. Juror's Award $200, Director's Award $150, Honorable Mentions receive catalogue. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $200 Juror's Award + $150 Director's Award + exhibition.

item.title: X ROID Bonn 2026 · The Stage Gallery
item.description: 7th edition of the international instant art expo dedicated to Polaroid and Fuji Instax photography. Three-day juried exhibition (May 29–31, 2026) at The Stage Gallery in Bonn featuring artist talks, a Pola walk, and creative exchanges. Only original instant photographs accepted — no prints. Accepted formats: SX70, 600, Spectra, 4×5, Packfilm, Polaroid Original, Impossible Project, Fuji Instax (all sizes). Fee includes professional framing. Gallery takes 25% commission on sales. Artwork uninsured during exhibition. In media partnership with Analog Forever. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: €225. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Defiance Zine Open Call · Revoke Collective
item.description: Open call for Revoke Collective's first zine on the theme of Defiance. Looking for photographs that challenge, disrupt, or simply refuse. Defiance can take many forms: quiet resistance, bold rebellion, personal freedom, cultural pushback, or moments of quiet nonconformity. Not chasing polish — chasing pulse. Raw vision and unfiltered moments. — Deadline: April 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Love & Romance Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: Online exhibition exploring how love has transformed alongside cultural and societal changes, and how those shifts shape personal experience today. Submit up to 3 images connecting the theme of love and romance. Virtual exhibition launches May 7, 2026. — Deadline: April 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: EDITION 502 — Open Call for Photo Edition
item.description: Open call for an independent 6×9 photo edition of 12 small photographs. EDITION 502 covers all design, production, and distribution costs. Author receives a percentage of sales. Looking for authors with a clear visual language and comprehensible concept, regardless of education or professional background. Submit 12 photographs with serial character, a cover sheet, and a text (max 2,400 characters). — Deadline: April 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Texture of Light · Pro Photo DC
item.description: Photography exhibition exploring light as a tactile, physical medium. Submit images where light feels like a material — surface tension on objects, atmospheric mass in fog or dust, architecture of shadow, or abstract luminescence through long exposures and macro work. Selected images will be printed and displayed matted and framed at Western Market in Washington, DC. Exhibition opens May 2, 2026. — Deadline: April 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Hariban Award 2026 · Benrido
item.description: International collotype competition combining 170-year-old analogue printing with contemporary photography. Submit 12 black-and-white photographs. Grand Prize: funded two-week residency in Kyoto collaborating with master collotype printers, solo exhibition, and publication in official catalogue. Juror's Choice and Benrido Award winners receive catalogue publication and free Collotype Academy course. — Deadline: June 15, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Residency + exhibition.

item.title: Atlas of Ruins Vol.3 — Call for Photos · Reuse Italy
item.description: Submit photographs of architectural ruins from anywhere in the world for the third edition of the Atlas of Ruins book. Photos can depict ruins from any historical period — abandoned buildings, crumbling monuments, forgotten infrastructure. Three registration tiers: Early (until Apr 16, €10/1 photo, €20/up to 10), Regular (until Jul 9, €13/€25), Late (until Oct 1, €16/€30). Fees exclude VAT. All participants receive an ebook copy. Best photos from each country featured in the printed book. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: €10–€30. Prize: €1,200.

item.title: LT5 Alternative Photography Show · KALEID Gallery
item.description: Open call for photographers working in alternative photography — including toy and plastic cameras, Polaroid, pinhole, photograms, and other alternative processes. Submit up to 2 works for exhibition at KALEID Gallery in San Jose, CA. Opening reception May 1 during South First Fridays Art Walk. Exhibition runs May 1–29, 2026. Contact curator via DM or email for submission details. — Deadline: April 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Film Photo Award 2026
item.description: Three grants of professional film and complimentary processing by Praus Productions. Open to emerging, established, and student photographers worldwide. — Deadline: April 26, 2026. Fee: $25–$35. Prize: $100.

item.title: Arte Laguna Prize 2026
item.description: International competition at Arsenale Nord, Venice. 120 finalists exhibited in 3,000 sq. meters. €10,000 first prize. All contemporary art media welcome. — Deadline: June 30, 2026. Fee: €97–€122. Prize: €10,000.

item.title: HNDL Magazine — PRIDE Issue
item.description: Submissions for the PRIDE issue of HNDL Magazine, an indie publication by and for neurodivergent, disabled, and chronically ill creatives. Accepting art, poetry, creative nonfiction, prose, photography, and zines. Especially seeking candid photography and creative nonfiction. Written pieces max 4 pages, no PDFs. Unpaid — contributors receive a printed copy. — Deadline: March 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Off The Clock 2026 · APA Los Angeles
item.description: 15th annual curated photo competition showcasing personal work. Juried by Chris Pichler, Founder and Publisher of Nazraeli Press, who selects 100 winning images. Winners receive a printed and PDF catalog, online gallery feature, social media exposure, and framed exhibition at an industry gala in Southern California. No categories, no series restrictions, no creation date restrictions — just your finest personal photography. APA members pay $20/image. No AI-generated content. — Deadline: March 31, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition + publication.

item.title: The Female Show 2026 · Munich Art Gallery
item.description: Group exhibition of national and international female artists at Munich Art Gallery in the Kunstareal, running October 15 – November 14, 2026, including Lange Nacht der Münchner Museen. Curated by Josephine Kaiser & Team. Seeks contemporary art by women beyond gender stereotypes and thematic clichés. Smaller formats preferred (up to 50×50 cm). Submit a PDF (max 5 pages, 5 MB) with short CV, artist statement, ~5 example images, Instagram and website. No participation or exhibition fees — only international shipping at artist's expense. Applications accepted in English or German. — Deadline: April 8, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.
